assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection turned trade theory into a framework that fits firm-level microdata. It reshaped how welfare gains, productivity reallocation and the effects of trade liberalization are analyzed, and it spread into macro, IO and development. The conceptual break is large and the empirical discipline is strong.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the core model. Helpman is central to the wider heterogeneous-firm agenda, including the Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple work on exporting versus FDI. Redding is an important extender through quantitative and spatial applications, but the founding contribution is more clearly Melitz and Helpman. The Krugman 2008 prize covered the earlier new trade theory, which makes this a natural successor topic.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of confirmation across many countries and datasets, with refinements and some debate over the gains-from-trade magnitudes. The framework is now standard in textbooks and policy models.
uncertainties: Helpman also appears under B030, so the credit split between his trade-politics and firm-heterogeneity work needs care.
Whether the committee prefers to credit Redding or the quantitative-trade literature alongside Melitz.
Quantitative gains-from-trade results are sensitive to the elasticity assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints and the financial accelerator explain how credit frictions amplify and propagate shocks. This is the core mechanism behind modern macro-financial models, and the 2007-09 crisis made its relevance plain. The contribution is foundational and has broad policy reach.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki-Moore (1997) is the credit-cycles paper. The financial accelerator was developed by Bernanke-Gertler and Bernanke-Gertler-Gilchrist. Bernanke, a prior laureate, is not on this ballot, so Gertler's role here rests on his own work and the accelerator lineage. Gilchrist is a strong empirical and quantitative contributor.
assessment.maturity: Nearly three decades old, widely confirmed in the empirical literature on credit spreads and investment, and extended in post-crisis models. The timing is mature.
uncertainties: Gertler also appears in B015, so the credit allocation across topics is blurred.
Overlap with the earlier Bernanke recognition may lower the marginal appeal of the accelerator branch.
Whether three names fit the credit-cycles story cleanly.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Misallocation across firms offers a measurable, quantitative account of cross-country TFP and income differences. It linked micro-level distortions to aggregate productivity and changed development and growth accounting and the policy discussion on reform.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh-Klenow (2009) is the pivotal paper. Restuccia-Rogerson (2008) is the parallel contribution, and Restuccia is credited on this ballot. The cleanest two-name credit is Hsieh and Klenow, though Restuccia is a serious alternative. I have a disclosed conflict: Klenow is a long-running co-author of mine, and I have not adjudicated this beyond judging merit on the evidence.
assessment.maturity: Fifteen or more years of replication across countries, with an extensive methodological debate over measurement error and the interpretation of dispersion. The framework has survived while its limits are better understood.
uncertainties: Measurement error in firm-level wedges may overstate the true misallocation.
Whether the committee gives credit to Restuccia and Rogerson as co-originators.
The interpretation of wedges as policy distortions versus other frictions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities underlies modern central-bank analysis and inflation targeting. It is a major intellectual synthesis with direct policy influence on a broad scale.
assessment.attribution: Credit is widely dispersed: Calvo (staggered pricing), Taylor (staggered contracts and the policy rule), Woodford (the integrated framework), Clarida-Gali-Gertler (the canonical NK model), and Christiano-Eichenbaum-Evans and Smets-Wouters (medium-scale estimation). Any three-name selection is arbitrary at some level. The Woodford, Gali, Gertler trio is the most coherent for the theory plus its policy implications.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and has been tested through multiple episodes, including the post-pandemic inflation, which has prompted debate over its limits.
uncertainties: The difficulty of limiting credit to three among eight names.
Debate over the empirical adequacy of the Phillips curve after 2021.
Gertler appears on two ballots.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and the trade-shock evidence changed the understanding of wage inequality, polarization and the local effects of trade. The work is empirically rich and has had large effects on both research and public debate.
assessment.attribution: Autor-Levy-Murnane and Autor-Katz-Kearney give the technology-and-tasks strand. Autor-Dorn-Hanson gives the China-shock strand. The task framework also owes a debt to Acemoglu and Autor, and Acemoglu was recognized in 2024. Katz's contribution is the long-run skill supply versus demand work with Goldin.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of work with some reassessment. The China-shock magnitudes are debated, but the broad lessons about adjustment costs are settled.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 recognition on technology and institutions and with Goldin's 2023 prize on labor markets.
The persistence of the China-shock effects and the identification debate.
Whether Dorn or Hanson is the more natural third name.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bayesian persuasion and information design opened a new branch of theory: how a sender optimally designs information. It has been applied in many fields, from markets and regulation to platforms and auctions, and it connects to mechanism design and robust analysis.
assessment.attribution: Kamenica-Gentzkow (2011) is the founding paper. Bergemann-Morris developed the information-design and Bayes correlated equilibrium agenda. Morris has a broader theory record in global games and robust mechanism design. Gentzkow also has substantial applied work in media economics that is not part of this ballot topic.
assessment.maturity: Fifteen years old and still highly active. The theory is established, while the empirical confirmation is thinner than in empirical fields.
uncertainties: Little direct empirical validation compared with other candidates.
The credit split between Kamenica-Gentzkow and Bergemann-Morris.
Timing relative to the maturity of the literature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The sufficient-statistics approach and the empirical taxable-income elasticity literature connected optimal tax theory to measurable behavior. The link between theory and administrative data has had a large effect on public economics and tax policy debates.
assessment.attribution: Feldstein's earlier taxable-income work is a precursor. Saez's optimal tax and top-income results and Slemrod's tax-compliance and avoidance work are central. Chetty's sufficient-statistics methodology is distinct but overlaps with his own mobility work on B037. Stantcheva is an influential younger contributor.
assessment.maturity: Substantial confirmation over two decades, although the elasticity estimates are contested and sensitive to identification.
uncertainties: Saez and Chetty also appear on other ballots, so the attribution is blurred.
The identification debate over taxable-income elasticities.
Whether the younger contributors have had enough time for a full assessment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: HANK models integrate household heterogeneity with nominal rigidities. They changed how monetary and fiscal transmission is understood, by emphasizing marginal propensities to consume and distributional channels, and they directly address a limitation of the representative-agent New Keynesian model.
assessment.attribution: Kaplan-Moll-Violante (2018) is the defining paper. The ballot names the three obvious authors. The broader heterogeneous-agent literature draws on Aiyagari, Bewley, Huggett and Krusell-Smith, where I have a disclosed tie through Per Krusell. Those names are not on this ballot.
assessment.maturity: Younger than the other candidates, with rapid growth but limited time for confirmation. Its place in the policy toolkit is still being settled.
uncertainties: It may be too early to judge the empirical validation and long-run influence.
The foundations lie in earlier work by others who are not credited here.
My professional ties to heterogeneous-agent macro are disclosed, but I have not adjudicated them.
